Kagesan wrote
A similar thing happened to me recently, when someone grabbed the ROM of my Bruce Lee remake, and ran it through Claude to have it slop-ported to Amiga and Atari ST. Last I checked, he was still asking for donations for all of "his" hard work on itch.io.
When I called him out for it, he finally bothered to contact me, and we made some small amends, but even after that, when he already knew well how I feel about it, he kept messing with my stuff, producing "enhanced" AGA and STE versions with horribly mangled variations of my artwork.


My support. I rejected those "remakes" because being slopware, but the real history is far worse. AI is destroying hobbies, homebrew and developper communities.

Author: vebxenon

segarule wrote
Well. like i hate hipocrisy i will leave some sinceres questions for i know if everything is running ethnic.

Quote
A similar thing happened to me recently, when someone grabbed the ROM of my Bruce Lee remake, and ran it through Claude to have it slop-ported to Amiga and Atari ST. Last I checked, he was still asking for donations for all of "his" hard work on itch.io.
When I called him out for it, he finally bothered to contact me, and we made some small amends, but even after that, when he already knew well how I feel about it, he kept messing with my stuff, producing "enhanced" AGA and STE versions with horribly mangled variations of my artwork.

The thing is that when we talked, he genuinely didn't give the impression of having ill intentions, and I absolutely believe him. There just seem to be people who can't imagine why someone wouldn't be okay with having his stuff fed to an LLM. It's freely available on the internet, and that's all the justification needed, apparently.
The guy who did this to your work probably thinks he's doing you a favor.

I really don't know where this will all end. The mutual respect between developers isn't something that applies to people always on the lookout for new stuff to feed to their LLM of choice, it seems, and the consequences are that a lot of communitues just find out that they have never been communities to begin with, rather two groups of people with little overlap, who just happened to gather around the same camp fire.

Personally, I hope Ed Zitron is right and the unsustainable financing of the AI bubble makes it crash rather sooner than later, removing the models from the hands of non-professional users. I just hope that the amount of digital asbestos that gets produced up to that point will not have killed what used to be the comfy niches of the internet entirely.

The code of Bruce Lee was created for Atari system that use 6502 processor. So obvious that my question no will make sense here. But the game have 2 authors:
Programmed by Ron J. Fortier
Graphic Art by Kelly Day
The SMS version mention Ron in title screen but not Kelly Day. The art cannot be created in SMS by Kelly Day but the art base yes. The characters, tilemap, map design. Kagesan you contacted the original author to use game design and art? Yes or no?


I feel this reply as insulting.

item.title: Made By AI :: RE: Warlord new game for Sega Master System!
item.description:
Author: AS_Games
Posted: Tue Nov 17, 2026 12:09 pm (GMT 0)

baude wrote
AS_Games: You shouldn’t make assumptions if you aren’t completely sure about what you’re saying. I say this with the best of intentions, because, honestly, I’m really looking forward to seeing more of your work.

Ichigo: Why the "LOL"? Lately, it feels like some of the forum veterans—a forum we all love so much and to which they have contributed a great deal—are being overly critical and harsh toward anything that deviates from the usual script. Not everything out there is bad; not everyone has ill intentions; and not every use of AI is a sign of laziness or a waste of time.


Yes, I know what I’m talking about because this is the reality of the present day; many people claim they don’t use AI, but they actually do. I see AI as a tool, just like any other. Without it, I believe that developing an engine from scratch in assembly which is what I’m currently doing would be an incredibly complicated and difficult task. I have great respect for all the veterans; after all, I am still a learner, and I’m very much in the process of growing and developing my skills. This game means a great deal to me it’s a dream coming true.

item.title: Made By AI :: RE: Warlord new game for Sega Master System!
item.description:
Author: ichigo
Posted: Tue Nov 17, 2026 12:06 pm (GMT 0)

You can do better than this "Bomberman" clone and ports.
There are many things I don't like about them, and obviously, the biggest one is that they are lazy ports/things (or mixes of several existing games).

At least use the power of LLMs to make new things, FROM SCRATCH.
With your own idea/universe.
Not some quick thing ripping music or gfx from existing games — a completely new game.

You'll certainly need to form a group, because gfx (pixel art) and music (PSG) have to be done by humans (LLMs are pretty bad at this; we're dealing with a basic 8-bit machine with heavy constraints, not a Switch or a PC).

At least AS_port showed us something new 👍

item.title: Made By AI :: RE: Warlord new game for Sega Master System!
item.description:
Author: haroldoop
Posted: Tue Nov 17, 2026 11:59 am (GMT 0)

baude wrote
ichigo wrote
I'm much less hostile to AI than some of my peers ;)

It can do some really great things, BUT we still have to point out that you need to prompt/steer LLMs very well to get the best out of them (and therefore be technical/know what you're talking about, because AI isn't actually 'magical').

So far, I haven't seen anything extraordinary.


Haven’t you noticed anything extraordinary—whether here on this forum or elsewhere?

In my view, Bomberman S and Megaman II, for instance, are on an extraordinary level. You can clearly see the work, effort, and a solid grasp of what an AI can—and should—be capable of doing.


Yes, those games are fantastic!
